newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE proposes 95/96 dividend of 1.50 marks.
newsitem.headline: RWE proposes 95/96 dividend of 1.50 marks.

text.p: German utility RWE AG said on Wednesday that it was proposing a dividend for the year to the end of June 1996 of 1.50 marks (98 cents) , up from 1.40 marks the previous year.

In a statement, the group confirmed earlier figures released in July that it had increased group net profit, stripped of minority interests, to around 1.2 billion marks in the year to the end of June 1996, an increase of ten percent.
The group also confirmed that group sales in the period grew 2.9 percent to 65.4 billion marks.
Earnings per share increased to 2.95 marks from 2.68 marks over the financial year.

RWE said that all of its areas of activity -- energy, mining and raw materials, petroleum and chemicals, waste treatment, plant and machinery, and construction -- had contributed to improved profits in the period.
The figures came after a turbulent day in which it said it was merging its German telecommunications business with fellow utility Veba AG and the British telecoms group Cable & Wireless.
Earlier in the day, RWE announced it was ending its telecoms alliance with fellow utility Viag AG and the British telecommunications giant British Telecom.
The group also said in the announcement that it was proposing to fuse two of its energy sector subsidiaries, Lahmeyer AG and Rheinelektra AG.
The proposal to merge the two companies would come before an extraordinary shareholders meeting in February 1997 for approval.
Shares in RWE ended bourse trade on the DAX index in Frankfurt up 2.95 marks at 60.60 marks after the announcement that it was ending its alliance with Viag and BT.
The share ended electronic IBIS DAX trade at 60.12 marks, up 2.22 marks, one of the day's main gainers.
RWE said that from the start of April 1997, Clemens Boersig would take over the role of finance director on the board of RWE. Boersig is currently in management at Robert Bosch GmbH.

Other new board appointments include Thomas Geitner, moving from the boards of Lahmeyer and Rheinelektra, and Rudolf Schwan, from RWE Energie. Franz Josef Schmitt and Wolfgang Ziemann would retire from the board at the end of this financial year, RWE said.
